questions.question: Saroja Vaidyanathan received Kalidas Samman for classical dance in _____

• Kalidas Samman is an Indian award presented annually by the Madhya Pradesh government to individuals who have made significant contributions in the fields of arts, culture, and literature.
 
• **The Madhya Pradesh government** in India grants the Kalidas Samman, an annual arts prize.
 
• The prize bears the name of Kālidāsa, an accomplished writer of ancient India in Classical Sanskrit. In 1980, the Kalidas Samman was first given out.
 
• At first, it was awarded in four fields—classical music, classical dance, theater, and plastic arts—every other year.
 
• The prizes were given out in all four categories most years between 1986–1987 and 2008–2009; after that, it was only given to one recipient annually.

• He was a Scottish historian, economist, and philosopher.

• Mill's work is considered to be one of the most influential works on India during British colonial rule.

questions.question: The Northernmost range of Himalayas is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Inner Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in South Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau. It is home to the world's highest peaks, including Mount Everest. 
 
• The Himalayas are divided into three main ranges - the Greater Himalayas or the Himadri, the Lesser Himalayas or the Himachal, and the Outer Himalayas or the Shiwaliks. The Inner Himalayas is a sub-range of the Lesser Himalayas.
 
• The Inner Himalayas is located between the Great Himalayas and the Outer Himalayas. It is also known as the mid-Himalayan range and is characterized by steep slopes, deep valleys, and narrow ridges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Aravalli Range is a mountain range in western India, running approximately 800 km in a northeast-southwest direction across Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat. It is the oldest mountain range in India and is home to several wildlife sanctuaries and national parks.
 
• The Purvanchal Range is a mountain range in northeastern India, extending from West Bengal in the east to Arunachal Pradesh in the northeast. It is also known as the Eastern Ghats and is home to several important rivers, including the Brahmaputra and the Ganges.
 
• The Shiwalik Range is the outermost range of the Himalayas, running parallel to the main Himalayan range. It is also known as the Sub-Himalayas and is characterized by low hills, forests, and grasslands.

questions.question: What is the fiscal year period in India?

options.text: 1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year
1st April to 31st December of the same year
1st January to 31st December of the same year
1st January of a year to 31st December of the next upcoming year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A fiscal year is a 12-month period** used by governments and businesses for financial reporting and budgeting purposes. In India, the fiscal year period is from 1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year.
 
• The Indian fiscal year is also known as the financial year. It is used to calculate income tax, goods and services tax (GST), and other taxes and duties.
 
• In government accounting—which varies by nation—and for budgetary purposes, a fiscal year—also known as a financial year or occasionally a budget year—is utilized. Financial reporting by companies and other organizations is another use for it.
 
• Many jurisdictions have laws requiring businesses to compile and publish yearly financial reports, however, typically the reporting period does not coincide with the calendar year.
 
• Accounting records must normally be kept up to date, and taxes must be computed annually in accordance with tax rules, which often align with the fiscal year utilized by the government. Annual tax calculations are particularly important for direct taxes like income tax. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The British colonial government **established the** present fiscal year in 1867** to harmonize India's fiscal year with the British Empire's.
 
• India used to have a fiscal year that extended from May 1 to April 30 before 1867.
 
• The LK Jha committee suggested establishing a fiscal year that began on January 1 and ended on December 31 in 1984.
 
• The government, however, decided against implementing this idea out of concern for potential problems during the transition time.

questions.question: Article 25 to 28 of the Indian constitution provide for _______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian constitution** provide for **the Right to Freedom of Religion**.
 
• This means that every citizen of India has the right to practice and propagate any religion they choose.
 
• This right also includes the freedom to manage religious affairs and institutions, as well as the right to own and acquire property for religious purposes.
 
• The Constitution also prohibits discrimination based on religion, and guarantees that every person has the right to access and attend religious institutions of their choice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Culture and Educational Rights: **Articles 29 and 30 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities. These articles ensure that minorities have the right to conserve their language, script and culture, and to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• **Right to Equality: **Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right to Equality. This right ensures that every citizen of India is equal before the law and has equal protection of the law. It also prohibits discrimination on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
 
• **Right against Exploitation: **Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right against Exploitation. This right prohibits trafficking in human beings, forced labor, and child labor. It also prohibits employment of children in hazardous jobs.
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion: **Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right to Freedom of Religion. This right ensures that every citizen of India has the freedom to practice and propagate any religion they choose. It also includes the freedom to manage religious affairs and institutions, and the right to own and acquire property for religious purposes.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Urban was launched by which Union Ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Urban (PMAY-U) **is a flagship housing scheme launched by the Government of India in **2015 to provide affordable housing to the urban poor.**
 
• The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs is responsible for the implementation of PMAY-U. The ministry was created in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Urban Development and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation.
 
• The scheme aims to provide "Housing for All" by 2022, which means constructing 2 crore (20 million) houses for the urban poor. The beneficiaries of the scheme include slum dwellers, low-income groups, and middle-income groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PMAY-U has two components:** Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) - Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) - Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP). The former provides interest subsidy on home loans for the beneficiaries, while the latter involves public-private partnerships for the construction of affordable houses.
 
• The other options in the question are incorrect. The Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing the finances of the government and formulating economic policies. The Ministry of Human Resource Development is responsible for education-related policies and programs. The Ministry of Rural Development is responsible for rural development-related policies and programs.

questions.question: Which of the following unemployment is the result of depression in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclical unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** is a type of unemployment that occurs due to the economic cycle of expansion and contraction.
 
• During a depression or recession, the demand for goods and services decreases, leading to a decline in production and employment. This results in cyclical unemployment.
 
• Cyclical unemployment is a type of unemployment that occurs when the economy experiences a downturn or contraction.
 
• This leads to a decrease in demand for goods and services, and subsequently a decrease in demand for labor.
 
• Depression in an economy refers to a prolonged period of economic downturn characterized by low economic activity, high unemployment, and low consumer spending. Cyclical unemployment is a common feature of a depression as it is caused by a lack of demand for goods and services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional unemployment **occurs due to the time lag between a worker leaving one job and finding another. This type of unemployment is generally short-term and occurs even during periods of economic growth.
 
• **Seasonal unemployment **is caused by the seasonal nature of certain industries, such as agriculture, tourism, and construction. Workers in these industries may be laid off during off-seasons, leading to seasonal unemployment.
 
• **Structural unemployment** occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills of the workforce and the demands of the job market. This type of unemployment is caused by changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer preferences.

• As the 16th Attorney General, he took over the position on October 1, 2022.
 
• Venugopal K. K. was his predecessor. In2010, the Law Commission of India designated him as a member.
 
• In addition to serving as acting Special Senior Counsel for the State of Andhra Pradesh, he has appeared on behalf of the State of Tamil Nadu for the previous twelve years.
 
• Ram Jethmalani: He was a renowned lawyer and politician who passed away in 2019.
 
• Kailash Vasdev: There is no information available on any person with this name being appointed as the Attorney General of India.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankhar: He is the current Governor of West Bengal and has not been appointed as the Attorney General of India.

• The Indian government's primary legal advisor is the Attorney General of India.
 
• **Under Article 76(1)** of the Constitution, the President of India appoints the Attorney General, who serves for the President's pleasure.
 
• The appointment is made at the Union Cabinet's request. To be appointed as a Supreme Court judge, the Attorney General must fulfill the requirements.
 
• Thus, the Attorney General ought to have spent at least five years as a judge or ten years as an advocate in a high court.

questions.question: The Parliament of India is also known as ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sansad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Parliament of India** is **the supreme legislative body **of the country which consists of two houses - **the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).**
 
• The highest legislative body of the Republic of India is the Parliament.
 
• **The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People)** make up this bicameral legislature.
 
• As the head of state, the President of India possesses the authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha and call a special session of either house of Parliament.
 
• However, the Prime Minister and their Union Council of Ministers must provide their approval before the President may carry out these duties.
 
• Members of Parliament are those who have been elected or nominated (by the president) to either house of Parliament (MPs).
 
• The term "Sansad" is derived from the Hindi word "Sansadiya" which means "of or relating to a parliament".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Lok Sabha" refers to the lower house of the Parliament of India which consists of members elected by the people of India.
 
• "Vidhan Sabha" refers to the legislative assembly of a state in India which is equivalent to the Lok Sabha at the state level.
 
• "Senate" refers to the upper house of the Parliament of some countries like the United States, Canada, and Australia, but not in India.

questions.question: The ancient city of Dholavira, is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ancient city of Dholavira **is located in the state of** Gujarat**.
 
• Dholavira is one of the largest and most prominent archaeological sites in India, belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The city was discovered in 1967-68 by archaeologist Jagat Pati Joshi, and since then, several excavations have been conducted to uncover its rich history.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer is where Dholavira is located.
 
• It is the most well-known Indus Valley Civilization archeological site in India and one of the five biggest Harappan sites.
 
• It is situated on Khadir Bet Island in the Great Rann of Kutch's Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is a state in central India known for its rich cultural heritage and diverse wildlife. It does not have any significant ancient city belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• **Rajasthan** is a state in northwestern India known for its historical forts, palaces, and temples. It has several ancient sites belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization, such as Kalibangan and Ganeriwala, but not Dholavira.
 
• **Karnataka** is a state in southern India known for its rich history, art, and literature. It does not have any significant ancient city belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
